Competitor landscape: NO 2024-2026 paper found that reports skeleton-JEPA-for-clinical-gait or continual-JEPA-for-movement with a measured normative-reference drift. The 3 closest competitors are (1) MOSAIC 'Modality-Specific Adaptation for Incremental Continual Learning in Parkinson's Disease Gait Assessment', arXiv:2606.13258 (2026) - supervised incremental classification, not SSL/JEPA; (2) GenGait 'A Transformer-Based Model for Human Gait Anomaly Detection and Normative Twin Generation', arXiv:2604.01997 (2026) - one-shot transformer, no continual drift; (3) TOPO-JEPA 'A Topological Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Continual World Models', Zenodo record 21365501 (July 2026) - continual JEPA but topological/agentic, no body biosignal. Adjacent: AdaJEPA 'An Adaptive Latent World Model', arXiv:2606.32026 (2026, LeCun team) for continual-JEPA; Human-JEPA arXiv:2608.21160 for human-centric JEPA.

RESEARCH DIRECTION (recommended; distinct from the existing D1-D5 files, which fix the objective and vary readout/consolidation/application):

Title: 'What a Skeleton JEPA Predicts Determines What It Remembers: Recovering Signed Laterality and Temporal Dynamics by Moving the Objective from Static Position to Motion Fields, Under Honest Source-Video-Disjoint Retraining.'

One-sentence question: The audited model already exhibits two information losses - signed left-right asymmetry (learned R2 = -0.187, below the untrained-encoder floor of +0.147, while raw coordinates solve it at ~1.0) and temporal order (discarded by construction of the mean/std readout, and no motion-aware masking was ever used) - so does changing WHAT the JEPA predicts (static joint positions -> velocity/acceleration motion fields computed from the cached poses) and HOW it masks (joint-wise spatial infilling -> causal past-to-future segments) restore both, and does the recovery survive encoder retraining with held-out source videos excluded?

Why novel and why now: every 2024-2026 neighbor keeps the prediction target fixed and changes only the readout, the consolidation term, or the application. S-JEPA/MAMP/Skeleton2vec use position or masked-motion targets for ACTION recognition on unseen-subject action splits, never clinical gait; the continual competitors (MOSAIC, GenGait, TOPO-JEPA, AdaJEPA) never treat a pose world model's normative reference or signed asymmetry. This direction makes the JEPA objective itself (target semantics x mask axis x symmetry handling) the independent variable - the single lever the audit's two measured informative nulls both implicate - and reuses the project's pre-registered probes as endpoints, closing the audit's explicit 'no motion-aware masking (deliberate)' and 'temporal_readout/effective_rank never computed' gaps at the objective level rather than the readout level.

Decisive experiments (all cheap; reuse cached poses, SkeletonPatchEncoder/SJEPAGait, source_disjoint_probe, and laterality builders):
E0 - Reproduce the two deficits from frozen checkpoints (laterality null; readout order-invariance; fingerprint d0acc262) as the reference.
E1 - Motion-field targets: retrain Stage-0 (normal-only) and the full 5-stage curriculum replacing position targets with first/second-difference velocity/acceleration targets (same 528-token layout, EMA target, VICReg, group term); ~20 min/retrain.
E2 - Causal mask axis: swap the joint-wise spatial whitelist mask for time-wise causal future-segment masking to force past-to-future latent prediction (the world-model objective).
E3 - Symmetry ablation: remove VICReg covariance decorrelation on mirrored-joint pairs (and/or add an anti-symmetry/equivariance auxiliary) to test whether signed laterality is recovered.
E4 - Honest generalization: source-video-disjoint retraining ladder (GroupKFold by source video) reporting the transductive-vs-inductive gap on laterality, temporal, and condition-separation endpoints - the audit's #1 unmet requirement.
E5 - Downstream: the same ridge probe harness with missingness/provenance controls comparing position-JEPA vs motion-JEPA vs causal-motion-JEPA.

Both outcomes are publishable: recovery implicates the objective causally; failure pins the loss to the pose representation/readout and sharpens the boundary (a clean negative for a 'motor side of the loop' audience).

Feasibility: ~20 min/retrain; pose caches, self-contained model classes, source_disjoint_probe, and laterality builders already on disk; 3 days is ample. Fit: hits CFP topics 'foundation models for movement/motor control', 'self-supervised learning for biosignals', 'interpretability of biosignal representations', and 'evaluation protocols / measuring whether pretraining helps', squarely on the motor side of the loop. Risks: training-heavy vs the frozen-probe directions; must pre-register the motion-field definition, causal mask, and symmetry ablation before inspecting results; small source counts (1/2/2 canonical videos) cap folds at two and forbid population/diagnostic claims.
